description: Conformance corpus for host-to-sandbox value marshalling. Each case is a host value, given as JSON text so that a key spelled `__proto__` arrives as an own data property exactly as `JSON.parse` produces it, returned from a host binding named `value`. The sandbox evaluates `probe` with that return bound to `v`; the probe yields a string, and every runtime asserts it equals `expected` byte for byte.
notes: A key is data. Writing an own `__proto__` key with an ordinary property assignment runs the sandbox's prototype setter instead: the object is reparented, the key's contents become readable through inheritance, and the key vanishes from `Object.keys`. A runtime defines the key as an own, enumerable, writable, configurable data property, which is what the sandbox-to-host direction already does.
The binding manifest every runtime uses: `{ "xript": "0.1", "name": "marshal-probe", "bindings": { "value": { "description": "Returns the case's host value." } } }`.
Object keys in `hostValue` are written in code-point order, so a host whose JSON maps keep keys sorted rather than in insertion order hands the sandbox the same order every other host does.
The script a runtime executes is `(function () { var v = value(); return (<probe>); })()`.

cases.description: an own __proto__ key arrives as data and does not reparent the object
cases.probe: [Object.keys(v).join(','), Object.getPrototypeOf(v) === Object.prototype, Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(v, '__proto__'), typeof v.isAdmin, JSON.stringify(v)].join('|')

cases.description: an own __proto__ key keeps its position among the other keys
an own __proto__ key nested inside an object arrives as data
an own __proto__ key inside an array element arrives as data
an own __proto__ data property stays writable
an ordinary object keeps its keys, order, and prototype
